text:
Matthew Schaefer won the Calder last season and has somehow found another gear. He's 19, playing 27 minutes a night (up from 24:41 as a rookie) and scoring a point a game, 17 in 17. The Islanders get 53% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, six points better than without him, and he's 34th of 515 skaters in wins added by goals.

That's not luck dressing up a teenager. His goals match his chances, and the Islanders have scored 3.4 fewer goals than expected with him on, so if anything the results lag the play. Evolving-Hockey had him driving expected goals at the 99th percentile among defensemen last season while stuck with weak teammates.

For context, the defensemen picked first to third overall since 2005 had a median of 0.35 points a game in their first full season. Owen Power managed 0.44, Rasmus Dahlin 0.54. Schaefer is at 1.00 in his second year. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 36% of his shots come off the rush, double a typical defenseman. Watch the first seconds after a turnover: he's usually already gone.
headline: Matthew Schaefer, 19 and already the engine
